sources.title: 我是怎样使用 AI 构建 E2E 测试体系的？
sources.checked_scope: Article dated 2026-06-06; problem, five-stage workflow, Verify/Test, Green, and E2E execution sections.
sources.observed_point: The author describes TinyShip's three frontend frameworks by two databases, a Spec → Code → browser Verify → Playwright Test → Green workflow, 100% coverage of that product's critical journeys, and local E2E runs for selected change/release events.
sources.limits: Evidence of one project's workflow, not a universal coverage rule. Framework/database combinations and CI constraints are product-specific. The article's 80%+ token-savings figure gives no baseline, sample, prompt, or measurement method, so it is not reproducible here.

sources.title: Software Engineering at Google — Larger Testing
sources.checked_scope: Fidelity, gaps in smaller tests, integration/system tests, and browser/device testing sections.
sources.observed_point: Larger tests chiefly address fidelity gaps such as unfaithful doubles and real component combinations; higher fidelity brings cost and failure risk. Browser/device checks are one kind of functional test.
sources.limits: Supports choosing a higher-fidelity check for a named risk; it does not prescribe CourtWork's test-layer ratio, browser count, or release gate.

sources.title: The Practical Test Pyramid (Ham Vocke)
sources.type: Practitioner article hosted on Martin Fowler's site
sources.checked_scope: Acceptance-test levels and Avoid Test Duplication sections.
sources.observed_point: Acceptance checks can run below the UI when the design permits. When a higher-level test finds a defect, add a lower-level regression; push checks down where they add no unique confidence.
sources.limits: A general practitioner heuristic, not a CourtWork-specific suite shape or numerical coverage target. The article is by Ham Vocke.

sources.title: Playwright Test Agents
sources.checked_scope: Planner, Generator, Healer, inputs and outputs sections.
sources.observed_point: Playwright documents agents that explore and write a test plan, generate tests from that plan, and replay/repair failing tests; documented healer outputs include a passing or skipped test.
sources.limits: Documents test-authoring features, not proof that generated assertions or healing preserve product intent. It does not confer acceptance or release authority.

sources.title: Playwright Best Practices
sources.checked_scope: Locator guidance, user-facing attributes, explicit contracts, and generator locator priorities.
sources.observed_point: Playwright recommends resilient locators based on user-facing attributes and explicit contracts rather than CSS/XPath or DOM structure; its generator prioritizes roles, text, and test IDs.
sources.limits: Tool guidance only. A locator does not by itself verify durable backend state, accessibility conformance, or visual quality.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.checked_scope: Definitions of task, trial, transcript, outcome and agent harness; grader types; coding-agent evaluation.
sources.observed_point: The guide separates a run transcript from the final environment outcome, defines an evaluated agent as model plus harness, and notes model variability as a reason for multiple trials and outcome checks.
sources.limits: Supports separating capability evidence from deterministic UI evidence; it does not set CourtWork's trial count, acceptance threshold, or provider authorization.

sources.title: XState Test
sources.checked_scope: Current package notice and model-based testing examples.
sources.observed_point: The page says the prior @xstate/test utilities are now in @xstate/graph and that graph testing documentation is forthcoming; the displayed @xstate/test examples are for the beta package.
sources.limits: Transitional documentation is not a package selection or compatibility verification. No dependency was installed or tested for CourtWork.
